missing_key_points: Reciting what an AWS service does versus knowing when and why to use it are two completely different skills.
Candidates frequently freeze in interviews when asked to actually design a system despite memorizing service descriptions.
The three upcoming business problems will demonstrate three different domains and architectures using the same Decision Stack.
In job interviews, jumping straight to drawing architecture diagrams without clarifying the core problem and requirements will prevent candidates from getting hired.
Slow loading times directly cause users to abandon pages, resulting in lost revenue.
Once content is cached at an edge location, subsequent local requests do not make a round trip back to the origin S3 bucket.
Before a major launch on Lambda, engineers should load test, check concurrency limits, and request quota increases in advance.
If a DynamoDB table with Provisioned capacity receives traffic spikes exceeding capacity, requests are throttled and parts of the application will fail.
For an enormous planned launch that exceeds anything a DynamoDB table has handled before, engineers should check warm throughput and prepare the table for the peak.
If the startup grows and requires complex reporting across connected data later on, the database layer can be swapped out without rebuilding the rest of the architecture.
Developing an architectural mindset focused on trade-offs helps engineers get hired faster and progress more rapidly in their roles.
A key differentiator between senior and junior cloud engineers is the ability not to over-architect and knowing which brief details to fix versus leave.
Briefs and interview prompts often include contextual details intentionally to see if candidates get sidetracked down the wrong path.
Services in a private subnet can still make outbound internet connections if a NAT Gateway is configured, while remaining inaccessible from inbound traffic.

Overloaded servers failing to scale cause database connections to pile up until hitting the maximum connection limit, creating a chain reaction where drowning servers act as terrible database clients.
Compute issues must be stabilized first before diagnosing potential database issues like missing indexes, poor queries, or undersized instances ('fix the fire before redecorating the kitchen').
If inventory lookups required complex relational joins with supplier contracts and purchase orders, they should remain in RDS rather than DynamoDB.
Tracking business metrics like orders per minute and cart abandonment turns monitoring into a business tool that communicates system health directly to executive leadership in terms of revenue.
Alarms can trigger automated responses, such as auto-scaling policies adding servers before engineers read the alert, or paging on-call staff with pre-written runbooks.
CloudTrail tracks infrastructure configuration changes (such as modified security group rules or auto-scaling policies) to diagnose root causes if configuration mistakes contributed to an outage.

unsupported_claims: The scenario involves a 4,500-employee financial services firm
missing_key_points: Strict financial regulations require that document storage and transmission remain entirely within the company's private AWS environment without crossing the public internet.
Unlike Lambda, continuous Fargate containers can maintain open connections across documents, eliminating repeated connection and initialization overhead when processing thousands of files.
Without SQS queuing, batch document uploads (such as 200 reports uploaded simultaneously on Monday morning) would force the system to provision wasteful peak compute capacity.

Database writes are deliberately separated from the Fargate processing container so that containers handling untrusted external documents do not hold credentials to write directly to the production database.
Bedrock configuration allows swapping out underlying AI models for newer, cheaper, or better-performing ones without altering containers, queues, or databases.
The billing alarm is set substantially higher than predictable daily spending so it alerts within an hour if a container gets caught in an expensive retry loop on a corrupted document.
Relying solely on ClickOps is insufficient to secure high-paying cloud roles because real production systems require repeatable, automated deployment.
Infrastructure as Code files are tracked in version control, creating an auditable history of who made changes, what changed, when, and why.
Being able to walk through business problems layer-by-layer while justifying trade-offs distinguishes production-ready engineers from candidates who have merely memorized services for exams.
